## Acceptance criteria

**AC1 — the card exists and fires at the right moment.** A new `NOTIFY_REASONS` member plus **one** `notify()` call where a checkpoint turn is successfully created (`pollPrComments.ensureCheckpointTurn`). It must fire **when the real QA execution begins — BEFORE the Codex verdict/findings cards**, not after.

**AC2 — provenance, because that is the point of the card.** It must carry the **PR number** and the **exact 40-hex head** under review. **A card that says QA started without saying of what is worse than no card** — Warwick asked for exact PR/head provenance explicitly.

**AC3 — it is a CODEX-ORIGINATED card in the display sequence.** Follow the existing composer shape and header convention in `notify.mjs` (`🗣 Larry` / `🤖 Codex` / `🔎 Codex findings` / `↩️ Disposition`). **Larry must never author, paraphrase or mirror Codex content** — this card is emitted by the Tower path itself.

**AC4 — idempotent, like every other card.** The `notification` table is keyed on `(turn_id, reason)`. **A poll round that re-sees the same checkpoint must not re-announce it.** Prove the second attempt does not send.

**AC5 — non-vacuity by execution.** Extend `test/notify.test.mjs`: the new reason is accepted, an unknown reason is still **rejected** (`NOTIFY_REASONS` is frozen and validated at `notify.mjs:59` — do not weaken that), and the composed text contains the PR and the full head. **Report the assertion count, never the exit code alone.**

**AC6 — no behaviour change to the existing four cards.** Their content, ordering and reasons are untouched. Report the before/after test counts.

> **⛔ SCOPE — Warwick’s words: "the SMALLEST completion of the existing display-only Tower QA journey."** No new mechanism, no Telegram input surface, no chat bridge, no agent bus, no artificial rounds. **Do NOT touch `mergeCheck.mjs`’s `round = 1`** — Mack established `merge_check_run` does not exist in the store, so that path has never run and is irrelevant here. Warwick ruled it stays untouched unless execution proves it blocks this sequence.

## AMENDMENT 1 — Larry, 2026-08-07, answering Keel's `CLARIFY`

**The read-back found my emission point was wrong for Warwick's literal requirement. Both decisions go Keel's way.**

### M1 — **OPTION 2. `watcher.mjs` is added to `file_surface` for ONE `notify()` call.**

**Warwick's words are literal: *"emitted when the real Codex QA execution begins."*** Keel established that `ensureCheckpointTurn` is where a round is **requested**, not where Codex **executes**, and named **five** recorded ways the QA never runs after that point — the fail-closed findings gate, an unreadable skill file, **unresolved git evidence**, `detectMergeClass` not firing, and `claimOne` returning null.

**Option 1 would have shipped a card announcing a run that may never start, on the one channel Warwick cannot reply through.** That is the order's own stated failure mode — *"a card saying QA started without saying of what is worse than no card"* — in a worse shape: **a card asserting a state that is false.**

**Emit inside `processTurn`, immediately before `doReview` / `doMergeReview`** — past the disposition gate, with `turnRow.pr_number` and `turnRow.head_sha` in hand, on the **real turn id**, ahead of `fireTriggers` by construction. **This also covers every QA origin, not just checkpoint comments** — `loop.mjs`, `bridge-ingest.mjs` and `seed.mjs` currently produce the four verdict cards with no started card, and Option 2 fixes that too.

**Two constraints Keel proved and which are now binding on the implementation:**

1. **The card MUST carry the real turn id. Never `null`.** SQLite treats each NULL as distinct in the unique index, so a `null` turn id would **re-announce every poll round, forever**. This is the one genuine double-fire vector.
2. **The call must be UNCONDITIONAL — not gated on `checkpoint.created === true`.** A crash between the turn insert and the notification insert would leave `created === false` on every later round and **the card would be lost permanently**. Let the index be the idempotency, exactly as `notify.mjs`'s own header demands: *"IDEMPOTENCE IS THE DATABASE'S, NOT THIS MODULE'S."*

### M2 — **GRANTED. `test/run-tower-loop-tests.mjs` added** so AC4 is provable by execution.

Keel was right that the declared composer-only test cannot prove DB-backed dedup, and right to refuse to cite an argument-from-index as executed proof.

### Accepted without change
- **C3** — runtime files are **content-identical, differing only in line endings** (CRLF vs LF, `core.autocrlf=true`). **Recorded so an alignment hash comparison is not misread as drift** — the same trap the map already carries for `sourceHash`.
- **C4** — dispatch head `58df36d` vs order header `6e7ed6e`: ancestor, all four canonical blobs identical at both. **No governance difference.**
- **C5** — clerical `document_impact` path. Noted.

### Unchanged
`round = 1` untouched · no supervisor or deadman · no Telegram input surface · **do not touch anything under `~/.mypka/**`** — alignment and restart are Larry's.

**No second read-back required.** Proceed.

## AMENDMENT 2 — Larry, 2026-08-07. **Warwick's correction: this is NOT a new capability. Scope narrows.**

> **His ruling:** *"Stop treating Tower/Codex QA as a new capability to design. The 2026-08-05 TowerBot transcript is the acceptance baseline… That capability was already delivered and was the point of the previous Tower phase. Do not rebuild it, redesign it, replace its trigger model, alter `round = 1`, create a new conversation mechanism, or re-prove settled architecture unless execution shows an actual regression."*

### ① INVESTIGATION FIRST, as he required. Result: **no regression exists, and nothing is to be restored.**

- **A "Codex QA started" notification has NEVER existed in ANY branch's history.** Established by execution — `git log --all -S` across `qa_started`, `QA started`, `review_started` over `services/**` returns **nothing**. `NOTIFY_REASONS` has one touch in its whole history (`2b44a1a`, BUILD-014). **So it is genuinely new, not regressed** — which is why he authorised it separately, and why AC1–AC6 stand unchanged as the *smallest* addition.
- **The Larry-response card is NOT missing and NOT regressed either.** `composeLarryMessage` and `summariseLarry` already exist in `notify.mjs`, and the function's own comment records the ask they were built for: *"so the Telegram message shows LARRY'S SIDE of the Larry↔Codex dialogue, not just Codex's verdict (Warwick's ask: 'I have no idea what you are doing in response to Codex')."* **The mechanism was delivered in the prior Tower phase and works.**

### ② THE ACTUAL DEFICIENCY — found by execution, and it is one line of behaviour

`pollPrComments.mjs:215-217` sets **`larryResponse: String(comment?.body ?? '')`** — *"Larry's side is the comment, **VERBATIM**"*. `summariseLarry` then excerpts the **first 280 characters**.

**So the card renders whatever leads Larry's PR comment. Because his checkpoint comments lead with `@tower head:` / `@tower checkpoint:` / `@tower finding …`, the card shows RAW CONTROL DIRECTIVES instead of his reaction.** That is exactly what Warwick sees in the accepted transcript. **The defect is in what the card is FED, not in the card.**

### ③ AC7 — the smallest correction, and it is INSIDE THIS ORDER'S EXISTING SURFACE (`notify.mjs`)

**`summariseLarry` must drop `@tower …` control-directive lines before excerpting**, so Larry's plain-English prose surfaces regardless of where it sits in the comment.

- Strip **whole lines** whose trimmed form begins `@tower` — the directive vocabulary is already defined by the `HEAD_RE` / `FINDING_RE` / `CHECKPOINT_RE` patterns in `ingestComment.mjs`. **Do not parse or re-implement those patterns; a line-prefix test is sufficient and cannot desynchronise from them.**
- **Everything else is preserved**, including the existing code-fence and whitespace handling.
- **If stripping leaves nothing**, return `''` — `composeLarryMessage` already handles empty by sending only the Codex card. **A card reading "Larry: (nothing)" would be worse than no card.**
- **Tests in `test/notify.test.mjs`:** a directives-only comment yields `''`; a prose+directives comment yields **the prose**, with no `@tower` text; ordering is irrelevant — **prose after directives must still surface.** Report assertion counts.

> **🔴 WHY THIS IS A CODE CHANGE AND NOT A CONVENTION.** The alternative was "Larry writes prose first, directives last." **That is a habit, and habits decay silently — it would depend on Larry remembering, in every session, forever, which is precisely the durability Warwick says must not be required.** Stripping in the composer makes the plain-English beat **independent of comment ordering and of Larry's memory.** *(A route-level convention is retained as belt-and-braces, not as the control.)*

### ④ Unchanged and explicitly NOT touched
**No trigger-model change. `round = 1` untouched. No new conversation mechanism. No Telegram input surface. No supervisor. Codex cards remain generated by the existing Codex/Tower route — Larry never authors, paraphrases or mirrors Codex content.** **This is not a new Tower workstream; the prior phase already paid for the mechanism.**
